newsitem.title: TAIWAN: High Taiwan corn prices seen boosting profits.
newsitem.headline: High Taiwan corn prices seen boosting profits.

text.p: Profits for Taiwan's leading grain importers are expected to rise after domestic corn prices jumped 40 percent in recent weeks due to low inventories, traders said on Monday.
Taiwan's local corn prices rose to T$7 per kg on Monday from about T$5 in late December after disruptions in corn shipment schedules and reduced imports sapped the island's inventories.
Major corn-buying companies' import costs were about T$4.3 per kg in recent weeks, traders said.
"Many Taiwan corn shipments were delayed by earlier poor U.S. weather," a trader said.

He said the inventory was reduced further after Taiwan's Cheng-I Food, a corn oil processor which imported about 630,000 tonnes of corn a year, dropped out of the market in November over financial problems.
Taiwan's corn inventories stayed at a low level earlier last week -- with 3,263 tonnes at Kaohsiung port and 1,425 tonnes at Taichung port.
Traders said inventories at the two major ports have recovered slightly by Monday, but not in time to lower prices.
Local surveyors reported that inventories in Kaohsiung and Taichung had risen to about 58,000 tonnes and 8,200 tonnes, respectively, by Monday, traders said.
"The new corn shipments are arriving," a corn buyer said.
The buyer said corn prices will remain high until the middle of February due to the delay between shipments arriving at the ports and the products actually hitting the market.
Hui Shung Agriculture Corp, Great Wall Enterprise and Charoen Pokphand Corp are among the major Taiwan corn importers which would benefit from the high domestic corn prices, a trader said.
"The three companies have more corn stocks in hand and they can sell some holdings to the market for big profits," he said.
Boosted by the major firms' expected profit increases, the food sector in Taiwan's stock market surged by 2.37 percent in Monday's trading, compared with a 1.40 percent rise in the overall index.
Hui Shung was up T$1.8 or the daily seven-percent limit to T$28, Charoen Pokphand gained T$1.2 to T$23 and Great Wall rose T$0.9 to T$23.4.
